craft_notes: Sthāyin: the license — surplus speech admitted. Sanskrit-first: riktasya jantoḥ kept the empty-being frame; alam anyena kept the dismissal-closure (enough-by-another). Rows: 1 ('enough by another' closes — alam end-weight, the āgama adopted only where fruit stands), 9 (any-recognition-taken-as-proof pair). Close: 'enough by another.' Rejected: 'sufficient by other means' — killed: alam anyena is the closing shrug (the other means exhausted); 'surplus'→'excess' — killed: atiriktā kept surplus (it exists, it is licensed).

lines: taken as proof — scripture-authority is granted;
that scripture is relied on where
excellent fruit is: enough by another.
l4.sanskrit_cite: iti riktasya jantoḥ atiriktā vācoyuktiḥ tāsāṃ kāṃcana prasiddhiṃ pramāṇīkurvatā abhyupagantavyam eva āgamaprāmāṇyam iti sa āgama āśrayaṇīyo yatra utkṛṣṭaṃ phalam ity alam anyena

reads_against.argmap: What licenses the surplus verbal-connections? → Surplus speech is licensed by any taken-as-proof recognition; the āgama is adopted where the excellent fruit stands — alam anyena.
